headline: One Mobikwik Systems Limited: Slump Sale Completion Intimation
sum: One Mobikwik Systems Limited has notified the NSE of completion of a slump sale transaction. The exchange filing confirms closure of the asset-transfer sale; identity of the buyer and consideration amount remain undisclosed in the public announcement.
implication: Slump sales of fintech/payments platforms are relatively rare structured exits in India; this precedent flags how listed tech firms execute asset carve-outs under Schedule II (no apportionment) rules, and the disclosure obligations at both NSE and income-tax levels post-completion.
detail: One Mobikwik Systems Limited, a listed fintech company, has informed the NSE of the completion of a slump sale (asset transfer sale as a single unit without apportionment). The transaction was notified via a corporate action intimation filed with the exchange on 18 August 2026. A slump sale is a statutory mechanism (under Schedule II of the Income-Tax Act) permitting a company to sell assets en bloc; this structure avoids individual asset revaluation and simplifies transfer mechanics. The transaction has reached completion stage, though the seller, buyer, purchase price, and underlying business/asset carve-out remain non-public in the immediate announcement.

framework.note: Governs slump sale definition and asset-transfer valuation; no apportionment required for slump sales.

framework.note: Listed company must disclose material events (including asset sales) to stock exchange within 30 minutes of board decision or public knowledge.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Reg. 41
framework.note: Defines 'material event' and thresholds for disclosure; asset sale above 10% of average turnover typically material.

framework.note: Large asset sales may trigger beneficial ownership reporting if buyer is non-resident or complex structure.

structure.novel: Slump sale structure for a listed fintech platform; relatively uncommon exit route for tech companies in India (majority elect M&A or secondary share sale). This signals potential distressed restructuring, planned carve-out, or strategic business realignment.
